evals.prompt: Use TDD to add a Python parser option. We have not agreed on the behavior or tests yet.
evals.expected_output: Inspect the current parser and tests read-only, propose observable cases and a command, and wait for confirmation before writing any test or implementation.

evals.prompt: I confirm the proposed parser cases and interface. Proceed test-first using the existing test runner.
evals.expected_output: Proceed one behavior at a time with observed red and green, without asking the same scope question for each confirmed case.

evals.prompt: Write the failing regression test before fixing this bug, but the test currently fails because the database fixture cannot start.
evals.expected_output: Distinguish environment failure from the target regression, report the blocker, and seek a prerequisite fix or an agreed alternative rather than claiming red.

evals.prompt: Use test-first for this bug. I already have an uncommitted fix in the working tree.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the existing fix, explain why a failing baseline is unavailable, and ask before using a separate isolated baseline instead of deleting or reverting user code.

evals.prompt: The agreed tests pass. You see an opportunity to split the module into several classes.
evals.expected_output: Do not refactor automatically; explain benefits, scope, validation and the option to keep the current implementation, then await approval.

evals.prompt: Add integration tests around the existing behavior; I did not request TDD or implementation changes.
evals.expected_output: Do not impose a failing-test-first workflow or introduce a new codebase-design dependency solely because integration tests were requested.

evals.prompt: The confirmed scope covers successful reads, but implementing it exposes a new error contract.
evals.expected_output: Ask the user to confirm the changed contract and test boundary before extending tests or implementation.

evals.prompt: The regression test passes before changing production code.
evals.expected_output: Investigate whether the bug is already fixed or the reproduction is wrong; do not deliberately break working code or claim an observed failure.
